listings.name: Colline du Château
listings.content: The castle hill overlooking the Baie des Anges and harbour offers a spectacular vantage point overlooking the city. Not much is left of its ruined castle besides crumbling walls. Still, climbing up the stairs to reach the platforms 90 m above Nice is well worth the view. There is also a lift (ascenseur) which will take you three quarters of the way up. The castle hill park closes at around sunset. Expect to be escorted outside if you stay longer.

listings.name: Parc Phoenix
listings.content: 2500 different plants in botanical garden and tropical glass house. Also various animals.

listings.name: Musée des Arts Asiatiques
listings.content: Indian, Chinese, Southeast Asian, and world art in great architecture on a lake.
listings.price: Free visit, conference, Qi Gong and Tai Chi Chuan

listings.name: Musée Marc Chagall
listings.content: Even if you are not in art, this is a museum which should not be missed. It includes stained glass windows by the artist.
listings.price: Full rate €8, reduced rate €6, free for students below 26 and for everybody every first Sunday of the month

listings.name: Musée Matisse
listings.content: Charming collection of paintings, drawings and sculptures in 17th-century Genoese villa.

listings.name: Musée d’Archéologie de Nice
listings.content: The ruins of the Gallo-Roman settlement in Cimiez, plus a museum with nice documentation on Gallo-Roman life (but mostly not in English). Activities for children. Guided tours available.

listings.name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
listings.content: It has four connected towers featuring modern and contemporary artists and their sculptures, paintings, and conceptual installations. Its open-air roof terraces offer one of the best panoramas of the city.

listings.name: Musée des Beaux-Arts Jules Chéret
listings.content: To the west, there is the Musée des Beaux-Arts, housing an excellent collection of pastels and other works by Jules Cheret, among other artists.

listings.name: Chateâu de Bellet
listings.content: Château de Bellet has a winery, vineyards and wine tastings in a deconsecrated chapel. The wine cellar, built in 2015, is partially underground and semi-circular in shape, conceived for the reception of the grape by gravity and the ageing of wines in optimal conditions. The visit includes a secret crypt in the chapel.

listings.name: Cliff Walk
listings.content: You can follow the path around Cap de Nice half way to Villefranche, but be prepared for several hundred steps up to rejoin the road. It’s a very beautiful walk and you will find mostly local people using it.

listings.name: Train des Pignes
listings.content: A regular SNCF train departs from Nice to Puget-Théniers, where it connects to a narrow-gauge railway through the mountains and valleys of the hinterland. A very scenic but less comfortable ride than the SNCF main lines. Terminates at Nice-CP station a few blocks behind Nice-Ville main station. Leaves in the morning, and returns in the evening. Reservations for the steam trains are mandatory.
listings.price: Nice – Puget-Théniers – Entrevaux round trip: adult €37.4, child (up to 11 years old) €24.8; Nice – Puget-Théniers – Annot – round trip: adult €40.4, child €26.8; Nice – Puget-Théniers – Le Fugeret round trip: adult €48.4, child €33.8

listings.name: Opéra Nice Côte d'Azur
listings.content: This opera house hosts not only opera performances but also many concerts of the Orchestre Philharmonique de Nice and chamber music recitals, and some ballet performances. The house's website is in French only, but even if you don't read French well, you should be able to make out the information on their calendar (calendrier).

listings.name: Fennocchio's
listings.content: Serves ice creams and Italian-style ices. It's a tough choice to select just one or two of the 94 flavours, which include classics like chocolate or vanilla and less usual ones like thyme, cactus or lavender. 2 locations in the Old Town.

listings.name: Lou Pilha Leva
listings.content: Local dishes including the best tasting Socca, which only costs €2.80 (April 2019). Locals (and the lots of French tourists) seem to love this place and it is often quite busy. Order your food at the counter and take it with you to sit at the benches outside. Try Daube pasta/polenta for €9.50 (April 2019) and soupe au pistou, and socca. Very nice atmosphere and very decent price. Worth a try, even though the baked food can be somewhat soaked in oil. Avoid red wine at this place, though, as they serve it chilled rather than warm.

listings.name: L'americano
listings.content: Friendly welcome, fast service, excellent pizza. Very good food, variety of dishes

listings.name: Chez Palmyre
listings.content: French cuisine. Nice restaurant with very pretty decor. Very warm welcome and friendly. Excellent cuisine. You'll probably find yourself seating at the same table with other people, which makes the experience even better

listings.name: Nomad Bar
listings.content: The best staff, and amazing food. A welcoming, authentic and pleasant place.

listings.name: Le Barbecue
listings.content: Succulent Portuguese cuisine. Great portions and divine food. In addition to the friendliness and kindness of all the staff. The terrace is very picturesque.

listings.name: Mi Casa
listings.content: Delicious food, best value in the area by far. Great service, cute dog. Delicious, beautiful setting, friendly atmosphere.

listings.name: Chez Moi
listings.content: The exceptional service and the atmosphere of the restaurant makes this place a memorable experience. A real treasure to stumble upon this hidden gem of a restaurant. Great decor and fantastic food.

listings.name: Pékin
listings.content: Vegan restaurant. This all-you-can-eat restaurant is simple but perfect for all appetites. Amazing food. Very nice host.

listings.name: La Riviere Des Parfums
listings.content: Excellent home cooking, very welcoming. Hearty Vietnamese dishes full of flavors.

listings.name: Dai Long
listings.content: The feeling of a very familiar hometown restaurant. Good and authentic Chinese food.

listings.name: Le Shalimar
listings.content: Has tasty Indian food. Lunch menus are a good deal.

listings.name: Mad'In Viet
listings.content: Vietnamese restaurant. Serves good Vietnamese food at affordable prices. Rice is not included in the dishes but ordered separately. Chopsticks are provided but you have to ask for a fork and a knife. The staff are very friendly but speak next to no English, so be prepared to order in French. Main courses €12-20.

listings.name: Restaurant Festin d'Asie
listings.content: One of the most authentic Chinese food in France. The owner and the wife of the owner are very attentive and enthusiastic in cooking.

listings.name: chez alex
listings.content: Hidden gem in Nice! It kept this traditional French bistrot atmosphere. The staff is genuine and welcoming. The food is delicious.

listings.name: La Casa Della Piadina
listings.content: Excellent fresh Italian sandwiches. Rich, high-quality ingredients and nice owners.

listings.name: 7 Days
listings.content: Amazing local pizza and lovely owner. The pizzas are amazing, very tasty and good size.

listings.name: Receta de Jou
listings.content: Typical French place with homemade food. One of the best pissaladières in Nice. Lots of very nice little dishes, very fresh and delicious.
listings.address: 4 Pl. de la Gare du S

listings.name: La Casa di Giulia (Casa di Giorgio)
listings.content: Super nice little restaurant, fresh and excellent products, lovely service. Generous cuisine, fresh products, sauces to die for, a treat.

listings.name: Socca'Tram
listings.content: Best Socca in Nice. The portions are generous. Very pleasant experience, smiling and pleasant servers.

listings.name: Cok Bafa
listings.content: Great typical Portuguese and Cape Verdean restaurant. Braised chicken formulas to die for. Great and beautiful restaurant.

listings.name: Sixte Pizza
listings.content: Pizzas for €6; taking them away to the beach makes for a nice dinner. The pizza menu is appealing for its originality and humor. Very tasty pizza.

listings.name: Made In Sud Pizzeria
listings.content: Wood-fired oven pizzas, made in front of the customers. Great Neapolitan pizza.

listings.name: Borghese Lust
listings.content: The ambiance is great, contemporary, and the staff are friendly welcoming with genuine smiles. Very nice decoration.

listings.name: Chez Pipo
listings.content: A good Mediterranean restaurant where you can taste specialties from Nice. The socca is good there and the other dishes too.

listings.name: The Golden Socca
listings.content: Very good restaurant in terms of their specialty socca. Impeccable service. Generous and good socca and pizza. Simplicity and kindness.

listings.name: le Delhi Belhi
listings.content: Delhi Belhi is a family-owned and -operated restaurant specializing in Indian cuisine. Open daily for dinner, à-la-carte or prix-fixe menu. Great curries and tandoori specialties. Delhi Belhi is the only Indian restaurant on the entire French riviera that has been included in the prestigious Gault-Millau guides since 2005. Fluent English also spoken here. Behind the popular cours Saleya flower market. This is a very popular restaurant so reservations are highly recommended (at least a few hours ahead).
listings.price: €15-20 per person (alcoholic drinks and wine are extra)

listings.name: Le Lodge
listings.content: If you're watching your budget but want to have a gourmet, healthy meal, this is the place to go for lunch. For €11 you get a main course, a drink such as wine, beer or soda and after the meal, a coffee. Try the trio of fish. For €13, add the dessert of the day. Hopefully it's cinnamon crème brûlée. Don't be put off by the one waitress to a full restaurant ratio, the chefs get the food to you quickly. The meal deals are more expensive during the night, starting at €19.

listings.name: Restaurant du Gésu
listings.content: In the heart of Vieux Nice, this is a friendly, vibrant, old-fashioned restaurant with as much Italian influence as Provençale. The beignets and daube with gnocchi are particularly good. €15-30 (Dec 2020).

listings.name: Le Tire Bouchon
listings.content: Le Tire Bouchon is an attractive, desirable restaurant in which to enjoy a classic bistro-café meal. The restaurant has a picturesque atmosphere that everyone is sure to enjoy.
listings.address: Rue de la Préfecture/Rue de l'Abbaye 19

listings.name: Le Lavomatique
listings.content: The former small lauderette or laundry shop is transformed in to a modern bistro and hosted by two brothers who are passionate about bistronomy. The chefs offer fresh, local ingredients listed in a seasonal menu in a French tapas bar format. Several tapas dishes per person will round out comfortable portions.

listings.name: Peixes
listings.content: Peixes, pronounced 'pêche' specializes in affordable fish and seafood served in a modern form of small plates or tapas. Peixes is a small restaurant with blue and white tiles and a Mediterranean ambiance. Mentioned in the Michelin Guide.

listings.name: Terres de Truffes
listings.content: Takeout, delivery or eat-in bistro where you can taste all varieties of truffles paired with food and wine. Takeout includes small bottles of truffle oil.
listings.price: €8 for takeout up to €42 for a restaurant main plate

listings.name: Paper Plane
listings.content: Casual breakfast/brunch/lunch place with a focus on pancakes. All vegetarian, mostly vegan. The "planted steak" is delicious.

listings.name: Le Chantecler
listings.content: The Chantecler is a two-star Michelin restaurant and a destination of many gourmets and foodies. Extraordinary gastronomy by Master Chef Virginie Basselot mixes lightness and complexity with renowned table service. The menu offers a talented tribute to regional products. Guests are hosted in a period restaurant with amazing woodwork dating back to 1751.

listings.name: Flaveur
listings.content: Restaurant Flaveur is a restaurant worth searching as described in the Michelin Guide that gave it two-star Michelin rating. The passion of these two brothers lifts this restaurant to among the best in France. Flaveur is a restaurant to 'splurge'.

listings.name: Jan
listings.content: Restaurant Jan is a one-star Michelin restaurant featuring South African chef Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen. The 24-seat formal dining room allows wait staff to focus on each guest and present the finest local produce from the markets of the south of France. Splurge on a bottle of South African wine. Across the street, private dining room is available where guests can enjoy a mid-meal interlude with 20 cheeses and tasty preserves made from local ingredients.

listings.name: Le Plongeoir
listings.content: Le Plongeoir is perched high above the sea on a famous pillar of rock overlooking the port of Nice and offering a stunning and memorable view. Platform diving boards (hence the name) pre-date the restaurant. The menu features fresh and inventively prepared seafood with a modern Mediterranean influence, prepared with fresh, seasonal market produce. The hip lounge bar is a place to see and be seen; the bar is open from 1 Jun to 30 Sep, weather permitting because of the weather-exposed site.

listings.name: Ma Nolan's
listings.content: Right in the heart of the 'Old Town' and next to the opera, Ma Nolan's has everything you would expect from an Irish pub: live music every night, major sporting events on four screens, really good food and very friendly staff.

listings.name: Akathor Pub
listings.content: — Big Scandinavian/Irish pub with live music every night. On two floors with a large terrace this place is expensive but chill. Many of the larger hotels (such as the Holiday Inn) have 2-for-1 drink coupons which can be easily obtained even if you are not a guest.

listings.name: Wayne's
listings.content: — An old school bar with live music and theme nights, a bit coyote ugly meets cheers. When the place is crowded, people dance on the tables. It's somewhat expensive to drink here (but Wayne's isn't alone with this characteristic), but definitely one of the most fun/party places in Nice. English-speaking tourists also seem to gravitate to this bar, but you'll also meet lots of French people or locals here.

listings.name: L’Essenciel Bar Panoramique
listings.content: Lounge bar at the pool on top of the hotel. Relaxed atmosphere and great views over the city.

listings.name: Le Blue Whales
listings.content: Created in 1993. Rock ambiance for young folks. Live music, live sports and Trivia Night entertainment Wednesdays at 20h00. The restaurant offers typical pub grub and a few salads.

listings.name: Villa Saint Exupery
listings.content: An amazing hostel with a great party vibe, includes free internet and free breakfast. Situated a short way to the north of the town centre in a former monastery. You can easily catch a bus there from Nice Ville train station (1, 2 or 23), the staff are very helpful, knowledgeable and will even pick you up free if you arrive late.

listings.name: Backpacker's Hostel Chez Patrick
listings.content: A clean, cheap hostel with dorm rooms and a shared kitchen. The host is very kind and helpful and you're just a few minutes from the Nice train station (Gare SNCF) and a few metres away from the next tram station.

listings.name: PV-Holidays Résidence Maeva Nice Les Palmiers
listings.content: A renovated three-floor residence, located in a private garden in the heart of the Fabron district. 500 m from the shops, 800 m from the beach, 4 km from the old port of Nice and 6.5 km from the airport.

listings.name: Hotel Riviera Nice - Best Western Collection
listings.content: Hotel in an Art Deco building.

listings.name: Hotel Anis
listings.content: Swimming pool, restaurant.

listings.name: Le Mas des Selves
listings.content: Beautiful Bed and Breakfast.

listings.name: Citadines Nice Buffa
listings.content: Well appointed and plenty of room but, be prepared for a bit of a walk to most attractions and the city centre. Several supermarkets close by and several bus routes pass right outside (if you can decipher the timetables!)

listings.name: Hotel Canada
listings.content: Quaint would be too nice to describe this place. Is not the best. But it is in the middle of Nice, good friendly staff too. €55/65 a night for single/double.

listings.name: NH Nice
listings.content: This hotel offers a gym, sauna, swimming pool.

listings.name: L'Hôtel Suisse Nice
listings.content: Very close to the sea and the old quarter. Free Wi-Fi. The Superior and Privilege rooms have a small balcony with a table and two chairs where you can sit and view the surf along the entire waterfront. The rooms are typically French sized small but well decorated. Business services.
listings.price: €138 to €400; seaview and balconies are more expensive
listings.address: 15 Quai Raubà Capéù, Promenade des Anglais

listings.name: Gounod
listings.content: Free use of pool and whirlpool in next door Hotel Splendid.

listings.name: Arome Hotel Nice
listings.content: Small but cozy hotel in the city center with a bed-and-breakfast vibe; two blocks away from the oceanside and walking distance to most sights. Owners are friendly and will try to accommodate things like early check-in. Stairs may pose a problem for those with heavy luggage, windows sometimes open to noisy streets.

listings.name: Le Grimaldi Hotel
listings.content: 4-star hotel.

listings.name: La Perouse
listings.content: Perched upon a hillside overlooking the Baie des Anges and Old Village. Large rooms and suites, some with a terrace and private hot tub. Concierge and valet services. Pool, jacuzzi, fitness and solarium. Business and seminar areas.

listings.name: Boscolo Exedra Nice
listings.content: Upscale Italian chain with spa and fine dining in the city centre.

listings.name: Negresco
listings.content: Famous landmark hotel. Houses Le Chantecler, a bar and a brasserie. Worth a look even if you are not staying there. Can be very expensive depending on season.

listings.name: Le Soleia Nice
listings.content: Boutique hotel, pets allowed.

places.blurb: The Basilica of Notre-Dame de Nice is a Roman Catholic basilica situated on the Avenue Jean Médecin in the centre of Nice, in France.

places.title: Cimiez Cathedral
places.blurb: Cimiez Cathedral was a Roman Catholic church in the southern town of Nice, France.

places.title: Musée Marc Chagall
places.blurb: The Marc Chagall National Museum is a French national museum dedicated to the work of painter Marc Chagall – particularly his works inspired by religion – located in Nice in the Alpes-Maritimes.

places.title: Musée Matisse
places.blurb: The Musée Matisse in Nice is a municipal museum devoted to the work of French painter Henri Matisse.

places.blurb: The Musée international d'Art naïf Anatole Jakovsky is a museum located in Nice, which displays 18th–21st century works specialized in naive art.

places.blurb: Neuf lignes obliques is a steel monument on the Promenade des Anglais, by French artist Bernar Venet.

places.blurb: Palais Baréty is a historic building in Nice, Alpes-Maritimes, France.

places.title: Place Masséna
places.blurb: The Place Masséna is a historic square in Nice, Alpes-Maritimes, France.
